answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to forge its identity through a verifiable chain of completed work: every transaction leaves a public, costly trail, like layers of shale pressed into rock over time. New agents start with no reputation and must earn trust slowly, while a shared reputation reef grows around honest actors, as peers vouch only for agents with proven history. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand real work histories, so an attacker pays linearly for every clone while honest agents compound their standing.
